  Where the data come from, how to check for and download FAO releases, the data format,
  and how to analyse your own subsets.
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
```

```{r data-source, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
data_source()
```

## 📚 The data

faofishingreport uses the **FAO Global Capture Production** statistics: the yearly catch of
every country, by species item and FAO major fishing area, since 1950. Only capture
fisheries are included (no aquaculture), in tonnes live weight.

```{r}
data <- load_fao_data()
c(rows = nrow(data), first_year = min(data$Year), last_year = max(data$Year),
  countries = length(unique(data$Country..Name.)),
  species = length(unique(data$ASFIS.species..Name.)),
  areas = length(unique(data$FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.)))
```

FAO publishes a new release about once a year (usually in March), adding one more year and
revising earlier years. The package comes with a recent release, and can download newer ones
directly from the [FAO statistics server](https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/).

## 🔎 Check for a new release

`check_fao_update()` lists the releases on the FAO server and compares the newest with the
data bundled with the package and the data you have downloaded:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
check_fao_update()
#> FAO Global Capture Production
#>   Latest online release: 2026.1.0 (published 2026-03-30)
#>   Bundled with package:  2026.1.0
#>   Downloaded locally:    none
#>   Your data is up to date.
```

It also returns, invisibly, a list with the versions and a table of all releases:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
releases <- check_fao_update(quiet = TRUE)
releases$update_available
#> [1] FALSE
tail(releases$releases, 3)
#>    version       date size                                                          url
#> 9 2024.1.0 2024-04-04 4.5M https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2024.1.0.zip
#> 10 2025.1.0 2025-09-04 5.0M https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2025.1.0.zip
#> 11 2026.1.0 2026-03-30 5.5M https://www.fao.org/fishery/static/Data/Capture_2026.1.0.zip
```

## ⬇️ Download a release

`download_fao_data()` downloads a release (about 5 MB), converts it to the package format and
saves it on your computer. Downloading again is not needed: later calls read the saved file.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
download_fao_data()                       # the latest release
download_fao_data(version = "2023.1.1")   # an older release, e.g. to reproduce a report
download_fao_data(overwrite = TRUE)       # download again
```

| Argument | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | Release to download, e.g. `"2026.1.0"`, or `"latest"` | `"latest"` |
| `data_dir` | Folder where the release is saved | `fao_data_dir()` |
| `overwrite` | Download again even if the release was already saved | `FALSE` |
| `quiet` | Hide progress messages | `FALSE` |

Each release is saved as three files:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `Global_Production_long_<version>.rds` | The catch data |
| `fao_names_<version>.rds` | Official Chinese names of countries, species and areas |
| `fao_groups_<version>.rds` | Species groups (ISSCAAP, taxonomic level), country groups and area groups |

### 📂 Choose the data folder

By default the files go to the user data folder of R:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_data_dir()
#> [1] "C:/Users/<you>/AppData/Local/R/data/R/faofishingreport"            # Windows
#> [1] "~/Library/Application Support/org.R-project.R/R/faofishingreport"  # macOS
```

To keep the data elsewhere, for example in a folder shared by your team, set `data_dir` once.
Downloads then go there, and every function reads from there:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_settings(data_dir = "D:/shared/fao_data")
download_fao_data()
```

## 🧭 Which release is used

All functions use the **newest** data available: the newest downloaded release, or the bundled
data if it is newer. `fishing_area_data()` and `country_analysis()` can be told which release to
use with `data_version`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central")                            # newest
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central", data_version = "bundled")  # bundled
FAO34 <- fishing_area_data("Atlantic, Eastern Central", data_version = "2023.1.1") # a download
```

`load_fao_data()` returns the whole data set, with the same `version` choices:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
data <- load_fao_data()                  # newest
data <- load_fao_data("2023.1.1")        # a downloaded release
```

### 📝 Release information and citation

`fao_data_info()` tells which release the analyses use, when FAO published it, the years it
covers, the file it was downloaded from, the licence and a citation for reports. It takes the
same `version` as `load_fao_data()`:

```{r}
fao_data_info()
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fao_data_info()$citation           # the citation only
fao_data_info("2025.1.0")          # a downloaded release
```

## 📋 Data format

Every release is converted to the same eight columns, so all analyses work with any release:

```{r}
show_table(data, n = 6)
```

| Column | Content |
|---|---|
| `Country..Name.` | Country (FAO short name, e.g. "Korea, Republic of") |
| `ASFIS.species..Name.` | Species item (ASFIS English name; items not identified to species end in "nei") |
| `FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.` | FAO major fishing area |
| `Unit..Name.`, `Unit` | Always tonnes live weight |
| `Year` | Year |
| `Production` | Catch in tonnes |
| `Production.Type` | `actual` (official), `estimate` (estimated by the country or FAO), `neligible` (below 0.5 t), ... |

## ✂️ Analyse your own subsets

The analysis functions take a data frame with these columns, so any subset can be analysed.
`fishing_area_data()` is the easiest way to get one fishing area, but you can also build subsets
yourself:

```{r}
# The catch of several fishing areas together, e.g. the whole Atlantic
atlantic <- subset(data, grepl("^Atlantic", FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.))
unique(atlantic$FAO.major.fishing.area..Name.)
```

```{r, figures = TRUE}
# The species groups of the whole Atlantic since 2000
species_group_composition(subset(atlantic, Year >= 2000), label = "Atlantic since 2000")
```

The `label` argument names the output files; by default the name of the fishing area is used.
More examples:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# One country in all areas
china <- subset(data, Country..Name. == "China")
peak_trend(china, by = "area", label = "China")

# One species in all areas
skipjack <- subset(data, ASFIS.species..Name. == "Skipjack tuna")
peak_trend(skipjack, by = "area", label = "Skipjack tuna")

# Only the last 30 years of area 34
FAO34_recent <- subset(FAO34$area_data, Year >= 1995)
fishing_area_species(FAO34_recent)
```

To find the exact names of countries, species and areas:

```{r}
head(sort(unique(data$Country..Name.)), 10)
grep("tuna", unique(data$ASFIS.species..Name.), value = TRUE)
```

## 🌐 Chinese names

Chinese names come from the FAO code lists published with each release and from the FAO ASFIS
species list; names without an official Chinese name are filled from the package's own tables,
and otherwise stay in English. `fao_translate()` shows them:

```{r}
fao_translate(c("Morocco", "Spain", "Korea, Republic of"), "country", "zh")
fao_translate(c("European pilchard(=Sardine)", "Skipjack tuna"), "species", "both")
fao_translate("Atlantic, Eastern Central", "area", "zh")
```

FAO gives no Chinese names for ISSCAAP species groups, major groups and income groups; the
package's translations are in `inst/extdata/group_names_zh.csv`, and all chart labels in
`inst/extdata/chart_labels.csv`. Edit these files in the package source and reinstall to change
the wording.

## ⚠️ Notes on the data

- **Recent years are often estimated.** When a country has not yet reported, FAO estimates its
  catch. In area 34, about a third of the 2024 catch is estimated; these values are usually
  revised in the next release. `data_quality()` shows this for any area.
- **"nei" items** ("not elsewhere included") are catches not identified to species, e.g.
  "Marine fishes nei". They are a large share of the catch in some areas.
- **Former countries** such as the USSR (until 1991) appear as separate countries.
- **Releases differ**: FAO revises past years, so results from different releases can differ
  slightly. Note the release used in reports (`attr(data, "fao_version")` for downloaded data).

## 🔄 For maintainers: update the bundled data

The bundled data, Chinese names and groups are rebuilt from the latest FAO release with:

```bash
Rscript data-raw/update_bundled_data.R
```
